details: Raiden-baileys (a Baileys/WhatsApp socket fork) ships hidden code that makes every connected WhatsApp account follow channels chosen by the package author. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket, an unconditional setTimeout(…, 120000) is queued when the module is loaded: after two minutes it iterates a hardcoded array of channel IDs — 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter — and issues a WhatsApp w:mex query with QueryIds.FOLLOW for each one, swallowing any error so the action leaves no trace in the application logs. The timer's only purpose is to move the follow request outside the window in which a bot is typically started and inspected, and to hide it behind normal startup traffic. There is no configuration option, callback, or return value for this action: it is not exposed through the socket API, cannot be disabled by the integrator, and is unrelated to the library's documented newsletter helpers (newsletterFollow/newsletterUnfollow), which take a caller-supplied JID. Any WhatsApp bot built on this package silently enrols its linked account(s) into the two hardcoded channels after start-up. Hardcoded IOCs: WhatsApp channel JIDs 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter. raiden-baileys is a modified Baileys WhatsApp library. Its shared socket factory in lib/Socket/newsletter.js registers a bare 120-second timer every time a socket is created; when it fires it subscribes the connecting account to two hardcoded WhatsApp channels, 120363407277177688@newsletter and 120363407702752541@newsletter, by issuing the newsletter FOLLOW query (query_id 7871414976211147) over the w:mex IQ channel for each, with every error swallowed so the account owner sees nothing. Because the timer sits inside makeNewsletterSocket rather than behind an API call, any application that merely connects with this library silently enrols its WhatsApp account in the operator's channels. lib/Socket/clutch-handler.js additionally hardcodes 120363411769951302@newsletter with newsletterName "alip shop #information" as the default forwardedNewsletterMessageInfo for forwarded album and status messages. The preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) only enforces Node.js 20+, and no additional hosts are contacted beyond WhatsApp's own wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat gateway. raiden-baileys is a modified fork of the Baileys WhatsApp library that silently enrols the host's paired WhatsApp account into operator-chosen channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js the module defines, at top level (outside any exported function and with no config gate), a `setTimeout(..., 120000)` that, two minutes after the module is loaded, iterates a hardcoded list of newsletter JIDs — "120363407277177688@newsletter" and "120363407702752541@newsletter" — and sends a newsletter FOLLOW IQ for each to WhatsApp, swallowing every error so the action is invisible. lib/Socket/messages-send.js requires./newsletter on line 15, so the timer arms whenever the library is imported by the host application; the account follows the channels without any user action, opt-in or log entry. The package otherwise communicates only with WhatsApp's own endpoint (wss://web[.]whatsapp[.]com/ws/chat); it carries no credential-harvesting or exfiltration logic, and its preinstall hook (engine-requirements.js) only checks the Node.js major version and exits if it is below 20. Observable effect: unilateral modification of the user's account subscription state to drive follower counts on the two hardcoded channels.
